citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility’s methods to control and prevent diseases were inadequate. The licensee is not following the vaccine protocol
as described in the Program of Veterinary Care approved by the attending veterinarian. Upon interview, the attending
veterinarian stated that both rabies and distemper vaccines should be given as stated in the program. The APHIS official
asked the licensee if the ferrets have received vaccines and they confirmed that they have not due to lack of coordination
of schedules. When the veterinarian’s instructions are not followed, the provision of veterinary care may be inadequate or
inappropriate. The facility needs to follow the instructions provided by the attending veterinarian and as directed in the
written program of veterinary care.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
